ABSENCE: nothing asserts that every candidate row's `direction` is one of the two expected literals, so a mislabeled row is dropped without any error or count

advisory.finding: A candidate row whose `direction` is neither 'fire' nor 'no_fire' (typo, or a future direction value) is silently discarded by `_selected`'s equality filter, so it contributes to neither side. Such a discard is invisible: a criterion whose candidates all carry an unexpected direction value collapses to zero selected rows and is reported as `skipped-unbalanced` — indistinguishable from a genuinely one-sided criterion or from the rows never having been present.
merged_from: Candidate-row field access is inconsistent between silent-skip and hard-crash: `_selected` tolerates a missing/unknown `direction` (silently filters), but `int(row["rank"])` (line 83) and `_input_descriptor`/`_dataset_case` accessing `row["tier"]`, `row["criterion"]`, `row["direction"]`, `row["rank"]` via subscript raise a raw KeyError/ValueError mid-emit when a candidate row is partial. A malformed candidate row thus either vanishes silently or aborts the whole run with an unhelpful KeyError, depending on which field is missing.
scenarios: Selector emits a candidate with a direction typo or a newly-added direction value
A criterion's candidates all carry an unexpected direction and it is silently reported skipped-unbalanced

ABSENCE: no path distinguishes 'zero candidates for this side' from 'candidate rows present but of an unknown direction'; the skipped_unbalanced verdict is produced identically in both worlds
advisory.finding: Malformed manifest rows are silently discarded: _read_manifest drops any candidate row whose `criterion` is missing/non-str, and _selected keeps only rows whose `direction` exactly equals 'fire'/'no_fire'. A row with an unexpected direction (or a candidate mis-tagged/missing criterion) becomes invisible, so a criterion can be reported skipped-unbalanced indistinguishably from a genuinely one-sided one — the balance check cannot tell 'no candidate on this side' from 'candidate present but unparseable'.
